item.title: Assistant Professor in Applied Economics at Erasmus University Rotterdam (the Netherlands)
item.description: The Department of Applied Economics at Erasmus School of Economics (ESE), Erasmus University Rotterdam, the Netherlands, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position, starting on 1 September 2027.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Applied Economics at Erasmus School of Economics (ESE), Erasmus University Rotterdam, the Netherlands, invites applications for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position, starting on 1 September 2027. The position is open to candidates with a strong research profile in any of our three fields: behavioural economics, health economics or strategy economics.

Our goal: Strengthen our research and teaching in behavioural, health and strategy economics, with research that helps firms, consumers and governments make better decisions.

Your colleagues: You will join one of our three sections, in a department with a vibrant research environment.

Job description

As Assistant Professor, you will join one of our three sections and do research and teach in that section. You are expected to publish in leading journals and engage in internal and external collaborations. You will teach in our bachelor and master programmes, and supervise bachelor and master theses. We also expect you to apply for external research funding, for example from NWO or the European Research Council (ERC). The department supports you in this.

Job requirements

What you bring

  • Academic background – You hold a PhD in economics. Candidates who are close to completing their PhD, or who already hold a tenure-track position, are also invited to apply.

  • Strong research profile – Your research fits one or more of our sections, and you show the potential to publish in leading journals.

  • Teaching ability – You are a motivated teacher, ideally with teaching experience at university level, for example as lecturer or teaching assistant.

  • Funding potential – You are willing to apply for external research funding.

  • Collaborative mindset – You value teamwork and collegiality, and you want to contribute to your section and the department.

  • Willingness to learn or ability to speak Dutch is considered a plus

Our main selection criteria are outstanding research potential and teaching ability.

Employment conditions and benefits

We offer you an internationally oriented and varied job in an enthusiastic team, with excellent working conditions in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO-NU).

The starting date of this position is 1 September 2027 and you will be based at Campus Woudestein, Burgemeester Oudlaan 50 in Rotterdam. This position is open for 1.0 fte. The salary is dependent on your experience and knowledge and ranges from a minimum of € 4.925,- to a maximum of € 6.682, - gross per month, scale 11 on a fulltime basis (38 hours), in accordance with the CAO-NU. Your position consists of a temporary employment contract as Assistant Professor on a tenure track for a duration of 6 years. At the start of the fourth year a department committee will formally assess whether you are on track towards meeting the final tenure criteria. In case you are on track, you already will be granted a permanent contract as Assistant Professor. After 5.5 years, a formal evaluation takes place with respect to research performance, teaching performance and contribution to the Department. When this evaluation is successful, you will be promoted to Associate Professor. When this evaluation is unsuccessful, your employment contract will be terminated at the end of year 6. In case of special personal circumstances, for instance combining work and care, the timing of the formal evaluation can be postponed.

Everything else we offer you, you can find below!

  • Everything you need for a good work-life balance: the option to work from home in consultation with your manager, 41 days of paid leave with a 40 hour contract, 8% holiday pay and an 8.3% end-of-year bonus, and a significant discount on a subscription for our on-campus sports centreOpens external!

  • Sustainable, inclusive and diverse work environment with an open culture, where you can be yourself and we pay attention to each other and to the world around us. Make the most of our bicycle budget, or join networks such as Young@EUROpens external, FAME or QuEUR.

  • Time and space for your development in the broadest sense: development days and a personal career budget and free access to our university library.

  • Good pension with ABP that EUR contributes 2/3rds towards, discounts on various collective insurances with Zilveren Kruis Achmea, Loyalis, and Allianz, and compensation for travel, working from home and home internet use.

  • Are you currently combining your job with parenthood, or do you want to do so in the future? EUR offers partially paid parental leave and fully paid additional birth leave for partners, and our campus features a daycare (daycare not paid for by EUR).

  • Moving to the Netherlands for your job with EUR? Then you may be eligible for the 30%-ruling if you meet the requirements of the Belastingdienst (Dutch tax agency), and with our Dual Career Programme we will also help your partner find the right job for them.

Employer

Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) is an internationally oriented university with a strong social orientation in its education and research, as expressed in our mission ‘Creating positive societal impact’. EUR is home to 4.100 academics and professionals and almost 33.000 students from more than 140 countries. Everything we do, we do under the credo The Erasmian Way – Making Minds Matter. We’re global citizens, connecting, entrepreneurial, open-minded, and socially involved. These Erasmian Values function as our internal compass and create EUR’s distinctive and recognizable profile. From these values, with a broad perspective and with an eye for diversity, different backgrounds and opinions, our employees work closely together to solve societal challenges from the dynamic and cosmopolitan city of Rotterdam. Thanks to the high quality and positive societal impact of our research and education, EUR can compete with the top European universities. www.eur.nl.

Faculty / Institute / Central service

Erasmus School of Economics (ESE) is a leading school in economics in the Netherlands. It has a strong international reputation and aims to do outstanding research. Moreover, it provides excellent education at the BA., MA. and Ph.D. levels. Much research at Erasmus School of Economics is policy relevant, has social impact, and offers a strong research culture, ample research resources, and comparatively low teaching loads.

Department

Our department

The Department of Applied Economics works on economic questions that matter for society. We aim for world-leading research that firms, consumers and governments can use. Our researchers are affiliated with the Tinbergen Institute, one of Europe’s leading research institutes and graduate schools in economics, econometrics and finance. They are also affiliated with the Erasmus Research Institute of Management (ERIM), where we work with colleagues from Rotterdam School of Management (RSM).

The department has three sections:

Behavioural Economics – We study how people make decisions under risk and uncertainty, over time, and in social settings. We want to understand what shapes behaviour, and we design interventions that help people make better decisions. Topics include health behaviour, financial decisions, security, and unethical behaviour such as lying and cheating. We combine decision theory with field, laboratory and online experiments.

Health Economics – We are one of the larger groups of health economists at a school of economics in Europe. Our main topics are health inequality, health behaviour, global health, social science genetics, and various topics at the intersection of health and labour economics. Most of our work is empirical, often using quasi-experimental methods and linked administrative data on the Dutch population.

Strategy Economics – We do theory-based empirical research on the organisation of firms, industries and markets. Our fields include applied industrial organisation, entrepreneurship, innovation, and regional and urban economics. The section sits at the intersection of economics and business studies, and targets top journals in both economics and management. Our staff also carry out studies for policy makers and industry.

There are many links between the three sections. We particularly, but not exclusively, welcome candidates whose work connects two or more sections.

Applying

Interested?

Please apply no later than 1 December 2026

Your application should include:

  • Curriculum vitae (CV)

  • Cover letter (max. 1 page). Please state which section(s) your work fits best: Behavioural Economics, Health Economics and/or Strategy Economics.

  • Job market paper

  • Research statement (max. 2 pages), outlining your research plans and how they fit the department

  • Teaching evaluations (if available)

  • Two reference letters

We kindly ask you to apply via the website (not by e-mail!).

Interviews will take place online in December 2026 and January 2027.

For questions about the position, please contact the head of the section closest to your field at our central emailaddress: apec-hiring@ese.eur.nl

  • Behavioural Economics: Georg Granic

  • Health Economics: Hans van Kippersluis

  • Strategy Economics: Jolanda Hessels

More about the department: https://www.eur.nl/en/ese/department-applied-economics

We look forward to getting to know you!

Erasmus University Rotterdam continuously strives to be an equitable and inclusive employer and invites all applicants, regardless of background gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, ethnicity, age, disability, or any other aspect that makes someone unique, to apply.

Recruitment and selection agencies or headhunters: thank you for your interest, but we prefer to recruit our candidates ourselves.

Link to job posting: https://www.eur.nl/en/working-at-eur/vacancies/tenure-track-assistant-professor-applied-economics-10-fte

item.title: Early-Career Agricultural Economics Fellowships (two positions) at Farm Foundation
item.description: Farm Foundation is seeking early-career agricultural economists for two separate 12-month fellowship opportunities in partnership with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA).
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
Farm Foundation is seeking early-career agricultural economists for two separate 12-month fellowship opportunities in partnership with the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). One fellowship will focus on regenerative agriculture, while the other will focus on bio-based products and maritime fuels.

Each fellowship offers an opportunity to conduct applied economic research, collaborate with USDA economists, and engage with leaders across food and agriculture.

Agricultural Economics Fellow: Regenerative Agriculture
Program Partner: USDA Economic Research Service (ERS)

The Fellow will examine the economics of regenerative agriculture, including farm profitability, adoption decisions and implications for agricultural markets and rural communities. Through applied economic research and stakeholder engagement, the Fellow will provide evidence to help farmers, industry leaders and policymakers evaluate the costs, benefits and tradeoffs of practices intended to improve soil health and agricultural resilience.

View the Full Regenerative Agriculture Fellowship Job Description

Agricultural Economics Fellow: Bio Based Products and Maritime Fuels
Program Partner: USDA Office of the Chief Economist (OCE)

The Fellow will study emerging markets for bio-based products, with a priority focus on maritime fuels. The research will assess opportunities for U.S. agricultural feedstocks and provide economic analysis to inform domestic investment, policy development and USDA engagement in international markets.

View the Full Bio Based Products and Maritime Fuels Fellowship Job Description

How to Apply

Interested candidates are encouraged to review the full job description for the fellowship that best aligns with their research interests and experience.

To apply, please submit the following materials to careers@farmfoundation.org:

  1. A curriculum vitae or résumé.

  1. A cover letter describing relevant research experience and interest in the specific fellowship topic.

  1. A writing sample.

  1. Contact information for professional references.

Please indicate which fellowship you are applying for in the subject line of your email and include how you learned about the position opening in the body of your email.

Application Deadline: November 30th, 2026

About Farm Foundation

Farm Foundation is an independent, nonpartisan organization that brings together people from across food and agriculture to learn from one another, explore complex issues, and put ideas to work. Our Agricultural Economics Fellowship invests in emerging economists whose independent analysis can inform decisions across food and agriculture.

Link to job posting: https://farmfoundation.org/2026/11/09/farm-foundation-seeks-applicants-for-two-agricultural-economics-fellowships/

item.title: (Senior) Policy Analyst for State Capacity at Niskanen Center
item.description: The Niskanen Center’s State Capacity team seeks at least two policy professionals of variable experience level to research, craft, and advocate for policies and practices that improve the government’s ability to turn policy into programs and programs into results.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Niskanen Center’s State Capacity team seeks at least two policy professionals of variable experience level to research, craft, and advocate for policies and practices that improve the government’s ability to turn policy into programs and programs into results. We are expanding our team and inviting applications from interested analysts or practitioners who have a demonstrated ability to produce high-quality public policy writing and have an interest in one or more functional areas in which we operate, such as: personnel management & the civil service, digital infrastructure and delivery, procurement, grantmaking, administrative procedure, et al. as well as a broader focus on public administration, bureaucracy, management, and leadership.

Description

Department: State Capacity
Location: Washington, D.C.
Schedule: Flexible hybrid, 2-3 days per week in-person; may require infrequent travel
Job Status: Full-Time
Experience: 3-10+ years of experience
Salary: $80,000 – $150,000, depending on level and experience, plus a generous benefits package
Reports to: Director, State Capacity

The State Capacity Initiative

The Niskanen State Capacity initiative advances reforms to make the U.S. federal government more capable, responsive, and effective at implementing policy and delivering on its promises.

Too often, legislators, advocates, and policy entrepreneurs work hard to enact a new statute or regulation only to see it crash and burn during implementation because the program couldn’t staff up, deploy technology, get clear direction from leadership, avoid procedural missteps, or manage fiscal flows. We see this as an urgent problem: our nation has many complex problems to solve and without better management policy and routines, the prospects of success in meeting those moments are dim. We work, as far upstream as we can get, to address these issues through innovative legislation, behavior change, and implementation guidance.

The Position(s)

We are looking to hire at least two policy analysts with specialized expertise in one or more of a wide range of functional areas (detailed below). Our priority is finding outstanding people with the skills to produce gold-star policy analysis and who can thrive in our collaborative environment. We invite professionals of various experience levels to apply.

Senior Policy Analysts are expected to independently cultivate relationships at senior levels inside and outside of government, lead large research projects, write model legislation, and look for opportunities for policy entrepreneurship across a complex stakeholder ecosystem. Senior Policy Analysts should be recognized experts in their functional discipline, speaking at conferences, writing op-eds, and bringing credibility to their work.

Policy Analysts are expected to, with coaching, do those same things, with the goal of becoming an independent operator and recognized expert over time.

Core Competencies

Regardless of functional focus area, strong candidates will have demonstrated excellence in:

  • Love of Government. You must care deeply about the public sector’s role in solving big, difficult problems on behalf of everyday people rather than special interests. You are not afraid to critique institutions sharply, directly, and in public when they fall down on the job, but you are motivated by a desire to make them stronger than ever.

  • Experience conducting original research and policy development. You have opinions about how the government ought to work, but are intellectually curious and follow the evidence where it leads. This might include generating new evidence where none exists. You seek to move beyond problem diagnosis to detailed policy recommendations that account for real-world conditions and trade-offs while aiming to be right on the merits.

  • Understanding of the policy ecosystem. You understand how decisions are made in Congress and agencies. You build relationships across the broader policy community and engender trust among those you meet internally and externally across our coalitions.

  • Outstanding communication skills. You are a strong writer who can move from short commentaries to full research reports, and write model legislative or regulatory text when appropriate. You can brief complex information persuasively to key audiences, including legislators and their staff. You are effective at promoting (or eager to learn how to promote) your work and opinions (e.g., on social media, traditional media, speaking engagements). Ideally, you can write engagingly about your areas of expertise for placement in magazines, external publications, and Niskanen’s journal Hypertext.

Functional Focus Area:

Policy analysts will work as part of a multifunctional team, tackling many state capacity issues and contributing to the team’s overall perspective on public administration and management. However, each policy analyst is expected to own a functional focus area and primarily drive policy change in that lane.

Accordingly, we are seeking strong candidates with credibility in one or more of the following topic areas:

  • New topic areas for us

    • Budget Formulation/Execution & Appropriations

    • Procurement (Both Contracting & Acquisition Strategy)

    • Oversight (GAO, IG, and/or Congressional)

    • Federal Financial Assistance (Grants, Loans, etc.)

    • Service Delivery & Customer Experience

    • State-Level Management Issues / State-level State Capacity

    • Executive Office of the President and/or Agency Structures

  • Expansion within existing areas

    • Public Sector Workforce & Civil Service

    • Technology and Digital Implementation

    • Administrative Procedure (APA, PRA, Privacy Act, etc.)

Have another focus area (or multiple) that you think fits with our interests but is not listed? Please apply and tell us about it.

Who Thrives at Niskanen

We are not a partisan institution, but we have a point of view that we pursue relentlessly: the Niskanen Center is driven by a vision of an America in which an open, pluralist society and democratic government enable all individuals to pursue opportunity, protect against risks, build community, and find purpose. This includes a government that is effective but liberally circumscribed, a robust social safety net as a component of a well-functioning free market, and an abundance of housing, energy, transportation, healthcare, and other necessities, the benefits of which accrue to regular consumers. This vision does not map neatly onto the two-party binary and neither do we.

Our colleagues hold strong convictions while staying intellectually open, are realistic about the policy process, and are committed to durable, bipartisan reforms. We care deeply about the role healthy, empowered public institutions can play in improving ordinary people’s lives. As a workplace, we practice what we preach: following the best evidence wherever it takes us, engaging in open and honest dialog, and inviting diverse viewpoints to the table in pursuit of actually getting things done.

How to Apply

Please submit a cover letter, resume, and writing sample (2,500 words maximum; published work preferred) combined into a single PDF. Applications are due by 11:59 p.m. ET on November 29, 2026, and will be reviewed after the deadline closes.

Apply here: https://jobs.gusto.com/postings/the-niskanen-center-inc-policy-analyst-senior-policy-analyst-state-capacity-07fe947c-6146-4cb2-afa9-4142cf0f93d7

Department State Capacity

Location Washington, D.C.

Schedule Hybrid

Experience 3-10+ years

Salary $80,000-$150,000

Link to job posting: https://www.niskanencenter.org/jobs/policy-analyst-senior-policy-analyst-state-capacity/

item.title: Fossil Fuel Transition Policy Advisor at International Institute for Sustainable Development (Canada, or remote in select Global South countries possible)
item.description: The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today’s greatest sustainable development challenges.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The International Institute for Sustainable Development (IISD) is a globally recognized think tank with more than 30 years of experience working to solve today’s greatest sustainable development challenges. We combine deep expertise across critical policy areas with a collaborative approach to research, advice, and hands-on support that delivers real-world results. Headquartered in Winnipeg, Manitoba, we are a diverse team of over 300 experts working from offices in Canada and Switzerland as well as other locations around the world. Our research and policy advice help governments, businesses, communities, and civil society make better decisions. Our international Energy Program works with partners across countries and disciplines.

We are currently looking for a Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, to work within the IISD Energy Program.

About the Position

The Policy Advisor, Fossil Fuel Transition, will work within IISD’s International Strategy team, helping governments and partners advance a Paris-aligned, just, orderly and equitable transition away from fossil fuel production and consumption, including reform of fossil fuel subsidies and public finance. We recognize the difficult choices facing fossil-fuel-dependent economies: protecting public revenues, energy security, jobs, and affordability while building more resilient and diversified economies. The role involves close collaboration with government counterparts, particularly in the Global South, and with researchers, intergovernmental organizations, and civil society, as well as other teams within IISD’s 50-staff Energy Program and other Institute programs.

The Policy Advisor will help design and implement applied research, policy advice, and technical assistance for countries seeking practical transition pathways. For example, the work may examine the effects of changing fossil fuel revenues on government budgets, assess subsidy reform options, or help translate national and international transition commitments into implementable measures. Key responsibilities include

Responsibilities

  • Leading policy-oriented research and analysis on fossil fuel transitions, public financial flows, macroeconomic and fiscal risks, subsidies, energy security and economic diversification; translating evidence into actionable options for decision-makers.

  • Designing and managing assigned workstreams and outputs, with clear workplans, responsibilities, quality checks, and milestones; coordinating partners; and contributing to reporting and budget management alongside financial project managers.

  • Building trusted relationships with government counterparts, especially in fossil fuel-dependent economies, as well as knowledge organizations, civil society networks and intergovernmental partners; adapting support to country needs and available evidence.

  • Supporting the development of more junior colleagues through clear task briefs, constructive feedback, peer review, and learning by doing.

  • Contributing to focused funding proposals and partner engagement that build on demonstrated demand and the team’s existing expertise.

  • Working with IISD Communications early in the process to turn research into clear, useful messages and products for intended audiences.

About the Successful Applicant

We are looking for a thoughtful, self-directed policy professional who combines analytical rigour with practical judgement and reliable delivery. The successful applicant can turn a complex policy question into a workable plan, communicate trade-offs clearly, and work constructively with colleagues across disciplines and time zones. They will understand that fossil fuel-dependent countries face real fiscal, political, and development constraints and will seek credible, country-owned transition solutions rather than one-size-fits-all prescriptions. This is a hands-on role with opportunities to take growing ownership and help develop colleagues.

Knowledge and Qualifications

The successful applicant will have (essential):

  • A bachelor’s degree or equivalent in economics, public finance, development studies, public policy, natural resource management or a related field. A relevant master’s or PhD degree is an advantage.

  • At least 5 years of relevant professional experience in macroeconomic or fiscal policy, applied economic research, public finance, energy policy, or fossil fuel transitions.

  • Strong strategic thinking, with examples of turning broad questions into concrete outputs and delivering projects to a high standard.

  • A sound understanding of the economic and fiscal implications of energy transition, particularly for countries dependent on fossil fuel production, revenues, or consumption subsidies.

  • Experience engaging government or public-policy stakeholders, preferably in emerging or developing economies, with sensitivity to local institutions, data and policy priorities.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce concise, persuasive policy notes or proposals for non-specialist audiences.

  • Proven project management: able to scope work, assign and follow up on responsibilities, manage deadlines, and flag risks early in international, multi-partner settings.

  • Experience providing constructive feedback, reviewing colleagues’ work or supporting the development of less experienced team members; formal line-management experience is not required.

  • A proactive and accountable working style: able to work independently, prioritize realistically, seek clarification early, and follow through reliably on commitments.

  • Resourcefulness and sound judgement about data and methods, including when to use government data, partner expertise, or specialist modelling rather than assuming one tool fits every task.

  • A collaborative, respectful approach across cultures and professional perspectives, with openness to feedback and a commitment to shared learning.

  • Excellent oral and written English. Proficiency in another language will be considered an advantage.

  • Availability to travel internationally.

The successful applicant could also have (desirable):

  • Experience in fundraising or preparing successful proposals, including translating funder feedback into clearer project design.

  • Applied experience in fossil fuel subsidy reform, public financial flows, economic diversification, transition planning or government-facing technical assistance.

  • Experience working with quantitative economic or energy-sector data or supervising specialist analytical work. Applicants with additional relevant experience who value hands-on delivery are welcome.

Position Details

Location: Remote, based in one of the following eligible Global South countries where IISD can employ staff: Burkina Faso, Colombia, Costa Rica, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Philippines, Qatar, Rwanda, South Africa, or Uganda; or hybrid in Winnipeg, Manitoba, Canada. The role involves regular online collaboration with colleagues and partners based in Europe and the East Coast of the Americas; reasonable overlap with agreed team meeting hours is required.

Candidates must hold appropriate work authorization in the country they are based in without any sponsorship from IISD.

Salary: Salary commensurate with experience and location.

Employment type: 80%–100% full-time-equivalent staff position, under an Employer of Record model.

This is a 1-year contractual position with a possibility of extension. 

Job Type: New

Application deadline: November 27, 2026, 4PM CST

Start Date: As soon as feasible

Application Procedure

All submissions must be in English.

Applications will only be accepted through Bamboo HR.

  • A cover letter (maximum one page)

  • A CV (no longer than two pages)

  • IISD Voluntary Self-Identification Questionnaire (optional)

Applications without a cover letter or CV will not be considered. Please include your availability and salary expectations in your CV.

Only those candidates we wish to interview will be contacted. Resumes will be kept on file for 1 year.  

IISD is committed to fostering a more equitable and sustainable world and welcomes candidates who uphold our values of diversity, equity, and inclusion. We encourage applications from individuals from historically underrepresented and marginalized communities, including women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, people of diverse racial and ethnic identities, and people of diverse sexual orientations, gender identities, gender expressions, and/or sex characteristics (SOGIESC).

We are committed to equitable and inclusive recruitment practices and to reducing barriers to employment and advancement. Hiring decisions are based on qualifications, experience, competencies, and organizational needs, while recognizing the value that diverse perspectives and lived experiences bring to our work. We offer reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and welcome applicants’ input on how best to support their participation. Candidates are invited to voluntarily self-identify and complete our employment equity questionnaire through our applicant tracking system.

item.title: Economic Fellow at NYU Institute for Policy Integrity
item.description: The Institute for Policy Integrity is seeking applicants for one or two full-time two-year postdoctoral research fellowships in economics, starting in September 2027.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Institute for Policy Integrity is seeking applicants for one or two full-time two-year postdoctoral research fellowships in economics, starting in September 2027. Ideal candidates should have a primary focus on (1) environmental or resource economics; (2) transportation and electric vehicle policy; or (3) energy economics/policy.

About the Institute for Policy Integrity:

Housed at the New York University School of Law, Policy Integrity is a non-partisan think tank dedicated to improving the quality of government decisionmaking. Our principal focus is U.S. energy and environmental policy, with a particular emphasis on climate change. We produce original scholarly research in the fields of economics, law, and regulatory policy. We also advocate for reform before courts and government agencies.

Policy Integrity’s interdisciplinary mission focuses on the rational use of economic analysis in government decisionmaking and how tools like cost‐benefit analysis and distributional analysis can improve policy design. Policy Integrity’s projects cover a range of issue areas, with a particular emphasis on federal environmental protections and federal‐ and state‐level electricity policies, as well as a steady stream of projects on public health and consumer protection.

Policy Integrity’s successful advocacy outcomes include ensuring that agencies are required to consider the lost social benefits and other harms of any deregulatory actions; guiding state utility regulators on the need to value environmental externalities in energy policy decisions; convincing both federal and state courts to endorse the use of the social cost of carbon for monetizing avoided climate damages; and prompting the Department of the Interior to analyze the option value of delaying offshore oil leases.

Responsibilities:

Fellows will focus primarily on comments in regulatory proceedings and policy and academic research related to environmental policy, energy policy, and natural resources management, but will also be free to work on issues related to benefit-cost analysis more generally. Fellows may be assigned to projects across a range of substantive areas or may be tasked to specialize in a key area depending on the economist’s experience and Policy Integrity’s priorities.

Fellows will work with Policy Integrity’s directors, attorneys, and fellows to prepare:

  • Policy reports

  • Comments in regulatory proceedings

  • Journal articles

Fellows are also encouraged to engage in independent research.

Requirements and Qualifications:

  • A commitment to advancing the mission of Policy Integrity

  • Ph.D. in economics or a related field by Summer 2027

  • 0-3 years post-doc work experience

  • Specialized knowledge in (1) environmental or resource economics, (2) transportation and electric vehicle policy, or (3) energy economics/policy

  • Excellent R or Python programming skills; experience in machine learning and AI applications is encouraged

  • Experience working with data

  • Excellent writing and editing skills

Policy Integrity is committed to a culture in which all people are welcomed, respected, supported, and valued to fully participate. We welcome and encourage applications from diverse applicants, and we consider multiple aspects of diversity.

NYU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and is committed to a policy of equal treatment and opportunity in every aspect of its recruitment and hiring process without regard to age, alienage, caregiver status, childbirth, citizenship status, color, creed, disability, domestic violence victim status, ethnicity, familial status, gender and/or gender identity or expression, marital status, military status, national origin, parental status, partnership status, predisposing genetic characteristics, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, unemployment status, veteran status, or any other legally protected basis. Women, racial and ethnic minorities, persons of minority sexual orientation or gender identity, individuals with disabilities, and veterans are encouraged to apply for vacant positions at all levels.

Benefits and Terms of Employment:

In compliance with NYC’s Pay Transparency Act, the annual salary range is $88,000–$104,000. New York University considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s work experience, education/training, key skills, internal peer equity, as well as market and organizational considerations when extending an offer.

NYU offers an excellent, comprehensive benefits package including generous paid time off and retirement contributions. Information about benefits can be viewed here. Partial relocation

assistance (exact amount based on distance) will be provided. Policy Integrity staff members also have access to academic enrichment opportunities at NYU School of Law, including some faculty workshops, colloquia, and other scholarly forums.

Policy Integrity follows a hybrid schedule that requires three days in our New York City office per week.

To Apply:

Interested applicants should send:

  1. a cover letter detailing your interest in the position and your relevant experience,

  2. a C.V.,

  3. job market paper,

  4. transcripts,

  5. a brief statement (less than one page) on how your background or experiences would enhance the diversity, inclusivity, and perspectives of Policy Integrity, and

  6. three letters of reference

All materials should be submitted through JOE. All materials must be submitted by the end of business day on November 27th, 2026.

Please send questions to policyintegrity.jobs@gmail.com with “Economic Fellow” in the subject line.

Link to job posting: https://policyintegrity.org/about/jobs/economics-fellow-2026

item.title: Survey Statistician at US Census Bureau
item.description: This vacancy is being filled via the Direct-Hire Authority (DHA) for a Survey Statistician position in the Center for Enterprise Dissemination located in any Federal Statistical Research Data Center within the U.S. Census Bureau.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
This vacancy is being filled via the Direct-Hire Authority (DHA) for a Survey Statistician position in the Center for Enterprise Dissemination located in any Federal Statistical Research Data Center within the U.S. Census Bureau.

This Job Opportunity Announcement may be used to fill other Survey Statistician, 1530-11/12, FPL GS-12 positions within the Census Bureau in the same geographical location with the same qualifications and specialized experience.

This job is open to

The public

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

Career transition (CTAP, ICTAP, RPL)

Federal employees whose job, agency or department was eliminated and are eligible for priority over other applicants.

Clarification from the agency

All qualified United States citizens.

Duties

  • Respond to questions from and/or provide assistance to the internal/external data user community.

  • Plan, coordinate, implement, and monitor project activities for large-scale research.

Requirements

Conditions of employment

OR

Combination of education and experience -- courses as shown in A above, plus appropriate experience or additional education. The experience should have included a full range of professional statistical work such as (a) sampling, (b) collecting, computing, and analyzing statistical data, and (c) applying statistical techniques such as measurement of central tendency, dispersion, skewness, sampling error, simple and multiple correlation, analysis of variance, and tests of significance.

AND

Specialized Experience: For the GS-11, you must have one year of experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-09 in the Federal service. Experience for this position includes:

  • Communicating in-person and in writing to diverse audiences or stakeholders;

  • Applying statistical techniques, methodology, or methods;

  • Assisting developing research plans or conducting research using survey, administrative, or public-use data;

  • Writing reports, papers or presentations that document or summarize research findings.

Applicants must demonstrate and provide evidence in at least 3 of the above areas to be qualified.

OR

Education: 3 years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree.

Specialized Experience: For the GS-12, you must have one year of experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-11 in the Federal service. Experience for this position includes:

  • Communicating in-person and in writing to diverse audiences or stakeholders;

  • Applying statistical techniques, methodology, or methods;

  • Authoring/co-authoring academic papers, publications, or reports that summarize/document research findings;

  • Providing project or research guidance regarding data collection, analysis, and/or interpretation, and proposing recommendations.

Applicants must demonstrate and provide evidence in at least 4 of the above areas to be qualified.

Education cannot be substituted for experience at this grade level.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer.

item.description: We have the power of over 50,000 students and co-workers.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
We have the power of over 50,000 students and co-workers. Students who provide hope for the future. Co-workers who contribute to Linköping University meeting challenges of today. Our fundamental values rest on credibility, trust and security. By having the courage to think freely and innovate, our actions together, large and small, contribute to a better world. We look forward to receiving your application!

Are you interested in the potential of citizens’ assemblies and other democratic innovations to drive climate transformation? Come join us!

Work assignments

The Environmental Change division (tema Miljöförändring) at the Department of Thematic Studies is looking to hire a two-year postdoctoral researcher specializing in democratic innovations.

You will be part of the Formas-funded research project Democratic Innovations for Climate Transformation (2027-2029), which entails a systematic and interdisciplinary knowledge synthesis of how climate citizens’ assemblies and related democratic processes can contribute to system transformation. The project explores what the existing research literature tells us about the political impact of climate assemblies, how they might contribute to broader systemic transformations, and what this means for Swedish climate governance.

As postdoc on the project, you will take a leading role in carrying out the systematic literature review across academic databases and grey literature, following established standards for searching, screening, and quality assessment. You will contribute centrally to the comparative synthesis of findings across studies, and to identifying evidence gaps in how deliberative processes connect to system-level transformation. You will also help design and facilitate stakeholder dialogues with Swedish municipalities and practitioners, which ensures that the resulting knowledge is robust and genuinely useful for policy and practice.

You will work in close collaboration with the project’s principal investigator and a research team from LiU and Stockholm Resilience Centre. There is considerable room to help shape the project’s methodological choices and analytical framework, and to co-author academic outputs arising from the review and synthesis work.

As postdoc, you will principally carry out research. A certain amount of teaching may be part of your duties, up to a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Qualifications

To be qualified to take employment as postdoc, you must have been awarded a doctoral degree or have a foreign degree that is deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree. This degree must have been awarded at the latest by the point at which LiU makes its decision to employ you.

Your doctoral degree should preferably have been awarded no more than three years ago. If there are special reasons, a degree awarded more than three years ago may be accepted. Special reasons include sick leave, parental leave, trade union positions of trust, service in the defense, or other similar circumstances, as well as service or assignments relevant to the subject area.

We are looking for someone with a doctoral degree in social sciences, humanities, or related fields, and a demonstrated familiarity with the research area of democratic innovations – for example, deliberative democracy, citizens’ assemblies, participatory governance, or environmental/climate governance. Experience carrying out systematic literature reviews and others forms of qualitative content analysis is considered a merit. So is prior experience with stakeholder involvement and co-production through workshops and similar formats.

You are curious, rigorous, and comfortable moving between the fine-grained work of systematic screening and coding and the bigger-picture task of synthesizing what it all means. You enjoy working collaboratively, taking initiative, and are able to communicate complex research to non-academic audiences, such as policymakers and practitioners. A strong command of written and spoken English is required.

The workplace

You will be employed at the Department of Thematic Studies where you will be affiliated with the Environmental Change theme. You can read about the workplace here.

Beyond the project team and the Environmental Change theme, you will also have the opportunity to be affiliated with LiU’s Green Democratisation Laboratory, a new research environment funded by Mistra (2026–2032) that explores how democratic innovations can strengthen public support for climate action amid accelerating climate change and political polarisation. This offers additional opportunities for intellectual exchange, collaboration, and engagement with a wider community of researchers working on green democratic theory, just transition, and participatory, deliberative, and arts-based methods.

The employment

This employment is a temporary full-time contract of two years. Starting date is Januari 1, 2027, or as soon as possible.

Salary and employment benefits

At Linköping University, salaries are set individually and differentiated, in accordance with the applicable collective agreements (RALS/RALS-T) and the university’s salary-setting guidelines.

More information about employee benefits is available here.

Union representatives

Information about union representatives, see Help for applicants.

Application procedure

Apply for the position by clicking the “Apply” button. Your application must be received no later than 27 November, 2026.

Applications and documents received after the date above will not be considered.

Please attach your selected research publications electronically, in pdf or word format, in the application template. Research publications, e.g. monographs, which cannot be sent electronically should be sent in three sets by mail to the University Registrar at Linköping University, University Registrar, S-581 83 Linköping, Sweden. The publications must be received by Linköping University no later than the deadline for application.

Please note that printed publications will not be returned. They will be archived at Linköping University.

In the event of a discrepancy between the English translation of the job announcement and the Swedish original, the Swedish version shall take precedent.

item.title: Junior Economist in Regional Development Dynamics Division at OECD (France)
item.description: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is an international organisation comprised of 38 member countries, that works to build better policies for better lives. Our mission is to promote policies that will improve the economic and social well-being of people around the world. Together with governments, policy makers and citizens, we work on establishing evidence-based international standards, and finding solutions to a range of social, economic and environmental challenges. From improving economic performance and creating jobs to fostering strong education and fighting international tax evasion, we provide a unique forum and knowledge hub for data and analysis, exchange of experiences, best-practice sharing, and advice on public policies and international standard-setting.

The Development Centre (DEV) helps developing countries and emerging economies find innovative policy solutions to promote sustainable growth, reduce poverty and inequalities, address gender inequality, and improve people’s lives. The Centre facilitates policy dialogue between governments, involving public, private and philanthropic actors. Countries from Africa, Asia and Latin America participate as full members in the Centre, where they interact on an equal footing with OECD members.

Within DEV’s Regional Development Dynamics Division (DEV/RDD), the Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA) Unit at the OECD Development Centre provides regional and country-based analyses in the region. The work of the OECD Development Centre on EMEA (www.oecd.org/dev/africa) seeks to fuel policy dialogue and support reform efforts by providing innovative regional perspectives through the flagship projects including:

  • The Africa’s Development Dynamics flagship report is the product of a collaboration between the unit and the African Union Commission (AUC)’s Department for Economic Development, Tourism, Trade, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM).

  • The Revenue Statistics in Africa report which compares tax and non-tax revenue statistics for 38 countries in Africa.

  • The International Economic Forum on Africa.

  • The Accelerating and Scaling Up Quality Infrastructure Investment in Africa (ASQIIA) project aiming to support African authorities in accelerating their infrastructure project cycles.

  • The AUC-OECD Africa Virtual Investment Platform (AVIP) aims to become the reference for comprehensive quality and timely information and analysis on public and private, foreign and domestic investment.

DEV is looking for a Junior Economist who will contribute to its work in the field of economic development research, with a focus on quantitative analysis. The selected candidate will carry out policy relevant economic analysis contributing to the thematic analysis of the annual report Africa’s Development Dynamics, and where relevant to the Unit’s and Centre’s horizontal projects. She/He will have experience in macroeconomic analysis, trade, competitiveness and industrialisation policies. The selected candidate will work under the joint supervision of the Head of Unit and Project Coordinator.

Job Description

Main responsibilities

Research, economic and policy analysis, and drafting

  • Carry out high-quality policy research on economic development in Africa.

  • Use quantitative methods to undertake economic analysis of the impact of policies. Conduct empirical analysis and evaluations of policies in national and comparative settings

  • Help coordinate the research, consultations, peer reviews, drafting, production, and dissemination of the Africa’s Development Dynamics report.

  • Contribute to the coordination and quality control of publications, reports and working papers of the Africa Unit, including the Africa’s Development Dynamics.

  • Prepare conceptual notes and related documentation for the annual International Economic Forum on Africa.

  • Draft high quality briefing notes, communications material, report presentations and briefs for senior officials related to relevant policy issues on the African continent.

  • Draft high quality research documents, project reports, blogs, as well as policy briefs and articles targeted at both technical and non-technical audiences and the media, under tight deadlines.

  • Support junior staff such as interns, guiding their work and providing feedback.

Liaison, outreach and event organisation

  • Help maintain and develop relationships with stakeholders from government and partners including other international organisations, think tanks, and agencies, such as the AUC, EU, AUDA-NEPAD, ACBF, ACET, BMZ, GIZ, foundations and academic networks.

  • Contribute to the development of effective consultations and dissemination strategies.

  • Participate in discussions in expert groups and assist in organising meetings, seminars, workshops, and conferences related to the work of the Unit.

  • In coordination with other team members, communicate key messages relating to the Unit’s work and specific projects within the OECD to external stakeholders.

Other duties

  • Respond to queries from internal and external stakeholders and partners in a timely manner.

  • Contribute to drafting project proposals to support fundraising activities.

  • Collaborate effectively with other colleagues and contribute, as required, to horizontal and multidisciplinary projects and other outputs of DEV and the OECD.

  • Keep abreast of economic/development policy issues related to international development, economics and globalisation to increase visibility and impact of the work of the Unit.

Qualifications

Ideal candidate profile

Academic background

  • An advanced university degree in economics (major in macroeconomics preferred) or relevant related fields. Training to PhD level would be an asset.

  • Good knowledge of macroeconomic policy and quantitative methods is required.

A specialisation in development economics or related fields such as trade, agricultural or industrial development would be a key asset, with a specialisation on the African continent or the member countries of the African Union.

Professional background

  • At least three years’ experience in applied economic research in the context of developing countries and globalisation, with a focus on trade, agricultural or industrial development in Africa

  • Proven record of analytical work, in particular applied economic analysis (analytical reports and/or published papers).

  • Experience in working in international organisations or think tanks would be an asset, preferably in an African country.

  • Experience in implementing policy-oriented research at the global level (e.g. in coordination with think tanks from developing countries) and in drafting technical reports on emerging issues affecting Africa, Europe and the Middle East.

  • Excellent analytical and drafting skills in English, the ability to meet tight deadlines, multi-task and produce concise, top-quality work at strategic and operational levels.

  • Excellent organisational, coordination and communication skills.

  • Accountability and autonomy: provide regular feedback to head of unit and project coordinator in an independent style.

  • Experience in organising missions and meetings, seminars, conferences and workshops with and for developing countries would be an asset.

Tools

  • Proficiency in the use of standard software applications (MS Office).

  • Good experience in the handling of data sources, econometric techniques and the use of statistical software (Stata, R, Python, Excel VBA, etc.).

  • Good knowledge and experience in using main statistical databases.

Languages

  • Fluency in one of the two OECD official languages (English and French) and a good knowledge of the other.

  • Knowledge of another language would be an asset (e.g. Portuguese, Arabic).

Additional Information

Core Competencies

  • For this role, the following competencies would be particularly important: Achievement focus, Analytical thinking, Drafting skills, Teamwork, Diplomatic sensitivity and Strategic networking.

  • OECD staff are expected to demonstrate behaviours aligned to six core competencies which will be assessed as part of this hiring processes: Vision and Strategy (Level 1); Enable People (Level 1); Ethics and Integrity (Level 1); Collaboration and Horizontality (Level 2); Achieve Results (Level 1); Innovate and Embrace Change (Level 2). Please refer to the OECD Core Competencies.

item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Leibniz Institute of Agricultural Development in Transition Economies (IAMO), the leading institute for research on agricultural and economic transformation in formerly centrally planned economies, and Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg, Faculty of Natural Sciences III, Institute of Agricultural and Nutritional Sciences, invite applications for the jointly appointed W3 Professorship for “Economics of international agri-food chains and trade” This position is combined with the roles of Head of the current Department of Agricultural Markets and member of the IAMO Board of Directors. It also contributes to the university’s profile lines, ‘Sustainability’ and ‘Transformation’. The appointment is to be made as of 1 April 2028. We are seeking a scientist with an outstanding record of research on the transformation of agri-food systems in formerly centrally planned economies from an agricultural, development, or other applied economics perspective. Particular emphasis will be placed on the interdependencies between transition economies and global markets in order to deepen understanding of the complexities of agri-food chains and trade amid economic, geopolitical, and technological change. Applicants should have a proven track record in relevant theories and methods related to at least one of the following areas:

  • Market and supply chain structures and price formation

  • International trade and geopolitics

  • Food safety and food security

  • Consumer economics

Experience in several of these areas and/or in IAMO’s target regions is preferred. In addition, candidates must have a strong background in modern quantitative methods (e.g., econometrics, structural economic modelling, including partial and general equilibrium models, data science, or choice experiments), as demonstrated by publications in leading international journals. Experience in transdisciplinary research and in building bridges between academic, business, and societal stakeholders is desirable. We are looking for a candidate with a strong commitment to fostering early-career researchers. Furthermore, applicants also bring a proven track record in leading research groups, developing research programmes, and securing national and international third-party funding. Knowledge of the languages and cultures of the study regions would be an asset.

We offer a stimulating, regionally specialised research environment with a strong network spanning all countries in IAMO’s study regions. The professorship provides excellent opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration within the university, particularly in the fields of agricultural and nutritional sciences and economics, as well as with non-university research institutes. IAMO also offers favourable administrative conditions for project acquisition, management, and leadership development, both within the institute and across the wider Leibniz Association.

Applicants must fulfil the appointment requirements set out in Section 35 of the Higher Education Act of Saxony-Anhalt. Particular emphasis is placed on a Habilitation in the relevant field or equivalent scientific achievements and recognition. Candidates are also expected to have appropriate teaching experience or qualifications. The professorship carries a teaching load of two semester hours per week at the Faculty of Natural Sciences III, specifically within the MSc programme in Agricultural Sciences and related degree programmes. The willingness and ability to teach in English are required. In addition, a cooperative, teamoriented working style and strong communication skills are expected. Further duties and responsibilities are set out in Section 34 of the Higher Education Act of Saxony-Anhalt.

Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg and IAMO are committed to diversity and to fostering an inclusive environment in which staff and students feel valued and inspired. In particular, we seek to increase the proportion of women among our academic staff and therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply. Both institutions are certified as family-friendly and support the reconciliation of work and family life.

Applications from candidates with disabilities are particularly welcome and will be given preference in the case of equal qualification.

Applications will be accepted only via the electronic Appointment Portal of Martin Luther University Halle Wittenberg: https://berufungsportal.uni-halle.de/

before 27.11.2026. In addition to a cover letter, applicants are requested to upload a comprehensive curriculum vitae (including their academic career history), academic certificates and transcripts, a list of publications, documentation of previous teaching experience (including evaluations), and evidence of successful acquisition of third-party funding. Applicants may also include information on significant roles or activities in organisations, as well as details of invited lectures, professional development courses, or additional qualifications. Applicants are further requested to submit a statement outlining their vision for future research projects—specifically projects that make use of and integrate with the research environment at MLU and IAMO (maximum 2–3 pages)—as well as a teaching concept (maximum 2 pages).

For further subject-related information, please contact Prof. Dr. Thomas Herzfeld (phone: +49 345 2928100, e-mail: herzfeld@iamo.de). Please note: Applications to this email address will not be considered.

If there are any questions about the appointment portal, please contact the Dean of the Faculty of Natural Sciences III and Chair of the Appointments Committee, Prof. Dr. Matthias Müller-Hannemann (email: dekanat@natfak3.uni-halle.de).

The Grantham Research Institute on Climate Change and the Environment is a world-leading centre for research on climate change, the environment and sustainable development at the London School of Economics and Political Science. Its work has been recognised through the award of the Queen’s Anniversary Prize for Higher and Further Education 2020–22.

We are seeking an outstanding and highly motivated Senior Policy Fellow to join Earth Capital Nexus (EarthCap) - an ambitious research and action initiative developing new approaches to understanding the interactions between climate, nature, the economy and finance.

The post holder will lead a substantial programme of rigorous, research-based, user-focused and policy-oriented macroeconomic analysis on the consequences of nature loss and climate change, and on the role of adaptation and resilience in supporting economic growth, fiscal sustainability, sovereign debt sustainability, price and financial stability and development. Working closely with the Executive Director (Professor Nicola Ranger) and a multidisciplinary team of researchers, partners and stakeholders, the post holder will shape and deliver an ambitious intellectual and analytical agenda that connects climate and nature to core macroeconomic policy frameworks and decision-making.

Candidates should have:

  • Considerable senior-level professional experience conducting rigorous, user-focused and policy-oriented macroeconomic analysis and engagement, including macro-fiscal, sovereign debt and/or macro-financial analysis.

  • Deep, hands-on expertise in macroeconomic and econometric modelling, with demonstrable experience developing, adapting or running models and interpreting model results and scenarios under uncertainty.

  • Demonstrable experience applying economic and quantitative analysis to climate change, nature or environmental change, adaptation and/or resilience, and translating environmental risks into macroeconomic or financial outcomes.

  • A track record of impact and engagement at a senior level, including substantial experience engaging directly with senior stakeholders in ministries of finance, central banks, international financial institutions, multilateral development banks, regulators or comparable policy organisations, and informing or influencing policy making or public debate.

item.title: Research Fellow for Greenhouse Gas Coalition at the Data Foundation (remote in US)
item.description: The Data Foundation is hiring an early-career Research Fellow to support the activities of the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Coalition.
item.dc:creator: Zoë Plakias
item.content:encoded:
The Data Foundation is hiring an early-career Research Fellow to support the activities of the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Coalition. The Coalition is convened by the Data Foundation’s Center for Climate and Environmental Data (CCED). It serves as a nonpartisan technical connector for the U.S. GHG measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification (MMRV) community. Its members work together to identify critical gaps, coordinate responses to shared challenges, and help decisionmakers access authoritative, reliable, and actionable GHG information.

The Coalition brings together 16 partner organizations, researchers from 13 universities, and former officials from 12 federal agencies and offices. The Fellow will support the Coalition’s operations, support its active technical initiatives, and maintain the shared field resources that help members build a common understanding of the MMRV landscape. These resources include the GHG Enterprise Catalog, a living map of the organizations, programs, data, and tools in the U.S. GHG MMRV landscape, and the State of the GHG MMRV Enterprise report.

This role offers an early-career professional broad exposure to the GHG MMRV field and a professional network spanning academia, the private sector, NGOs, and former government.

  • Term: Full-time contractor role from January through September 2027, with potential for extension pending funding

  • Compensation: $55,000 for the fellowship term

  • Location: Fully remote within the United States. The Fellow is expected to be available during Eastern Time Zone hours.

  • Travel: About two domestic trips and one potential international trip during the fellowship

  • Start date: January 2027

  • Applications: Reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled

PLACEMENT AND MENTORSHIP

The Research Fellow will sit within CCED and report to CCED’s Senior Director, who also serves as Acting Chair of the GHG Coalition. The Senior Director will lead day-to-day mentorship through regular one-on-one conversations, connections to senior leaders, and exposure to Coalition strategy.

The Fellow will also receive technical mentorship from members of the Coalition’s advisory board, which includes leaders in GHG measurement, monitoring, and inventories. The role offers hands-on exposure to the Coalition’s priority initiatives, including its technical working groups, a parallel CCED Research Fellow placement on the third Regional Carbon Cycle Assessment and Processes study (RECCAP3), and related efforts led by partner organizations.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Support GHG Coalition meetings and convenings

  • Support the Coalition’s advisory board with agenda development and preparation for strategic discussions

  • Provide operational support for Coalition initiatives, such as the Methane Plume Technical Working Group and the RECCAP3 process, as well as related efforts led by partner organizations

  • Help work toward the first public iteration of the GHG Enterprise Catalog, a living map of MMRV organizations, data, and tools

  • Contribute to the next edition of the State of the GHG MMRV Enterprise report

  • Build a national database of GHG instruments sitting unused in labs

  • Help convene a strategy workshop on the future of the U.S. GHG information system and document the resulting priorities

  • Coordinate with other GHG and climate data organizations in the MMRV community

  • Document Coalition processes for reuse beyond the fellowship term

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • 3 to 5 years of relevant professional or research experience

  • Familiarity with the U.S. GHG or climate data landscape through coursework, research, or professional experience

  • Experience organizing, tracking, or synthesizing information across organizations, programs, or datasets

  • Ability to synthesize complex information across multiple sectors and organizations

  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with attention to follow-through

  • Strong written and oral communication skills for technical, policy, and general audiences

  • Ability to manage time independently and deliver high-quality work on schedule

  • Authorization to work in the United States

Preferred

  • Master’s degree or Ph.D. in environmental science, public policy, atmospheric science, or a related field

  • Experience supporting a working group, coalition, or multi-organization network

  • Experience building or maintaining databases, catalogs, or data visualizations

  • Experience in or adjacent to federal climate science, data, or policy roles

If you do not meet every qualification but can accomplish the aims of this position, we encourage you to apply. The Data Foundation is an equal opportunity organization.

CLIMATE RESERVE PARTICIPATION

Funding for this fellowship is provided by Climate Reserve, an initiative of the Aspen Global Change Institute (AGCI). The Fellow will join a cohort of Climate Reserve Fellows. They will spend 20% of their time engaging with the Climate Reserve Coalition and the broader climate ecosystem. Specific activities will be outlined in a separate Fellowship Expectations Agreement. Potential activities include:

  • Climate Reserve virtual learning sessions, fellow working groups, and cross-coalition coordination

  • Peer-to-peer engagement with other Climate Reserve Fellows

  • Researching emerging developments, risks, or opportunities in the Fellow’s focus area and sharing findings

  • Documenting lessons learned or tools in short formats, such as memos, slide decks, or case studies

  • Networking within and beyond the Climate Reserve Coalition

  • Brief surveys or reflections on shared learning

  • Applying insights from Climate Reserve peers to the Fellow’s project or to new cross-organization initiatives

  • Attending the Climate Reserve annual convening

HOW TO APPLY

To apply, email sonia.wang@datafoundation.org with the subject line “GHG Coalition Research Fellow Application: LastName, FirstName” and attach the following as PDFs:

  • CV: LastName_FirstName_GHGResearch Fellow_CV.pdf

  • Cover letter: LastName_FirstName_GHGResearch Fellow_CoverLetter.pdf

In your cover letter, please describe:

  • Your familiarity with the U.S. GHG enterprise, including relevant coursework, research, or professional experience

  • Your project management experience, including how you have helped a team or network stay organized and informed, for example by tracking timelines and deliverables, maintaining shared resources, or documenting work

  • Why you are interested in this fellowship and how working with CCED, the GHG Coalition, and Climate Reserve would support your goals

  • Whether you are currently authorized to work in the United States

ABOUT THE DATA FOUNDATION & PARTNERS

The Data Foundation is a nonprofit organization based in Washington, D.C. that champions the use of open data and evidence-informed public policy to make society better for everyone. As a nonpartisan think tank, we conduct research, collaborative thought leadership, and advocacy programs that advance practical policies for the creation and use of accessible, trustworthy data. Our activities proactively address emerging data-related needs in the country with the goal of devising realistic solutions, accelerating policy coordination, and advancing innovation. The Data Foundation is recognized by Candid Guidestar with the Platinum Seal of Transparency and received 4-Stars from Charity Navigator. To learn more, visit www.datafoundation.org. (LEI: 254900143CTC59RFW495)

The Data Foundation has four core values that guide our work:

  • Transparency: We rely on facts and transparency to generate trust and credibility

  • Pragmatic action: We promote practical, timely solutions to data-related challenges. Our ethos is “See a problem, fix a problem.”

  • Radical collaboration: We enthusiastically pursue opportunities to foster non-traditional collaboration with people and groups that hold divergent beliefs and points of view to jointly identify and solve problems

  • Diversity, equity, and inclusion: We seek to embrace and include diversity in all of its forms in our work, and our belief is that through the use of data and research, more equitable opportunities and outcomes will be achieved

The Data Foundation’s Center for Climate and Environmental Data (CCED) works as a nonpartisan knowledge broker. It helps ensure decisionmakers can ground their decisions in climate and environmental data that is timely and fit for purpose. CCED leads the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Coalition. The Coalition brings together technical expertise from academia, the private sector, NGOs, and former government officials to strengthen and coordinate the U.S. GHG measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification (MMRV) ecosystem.

Climate Reserve (CR) is a field-building initiative designed to safeguard and modernize the climate capacity needed for scaled global action. Born from a moment of profound disruption, CR is building a durable community of strategically placed climate experts to sustain critical work across data, science, policy, implementation, and frontline communities, with an eye towards reimagining how knowledge, talent, and institutions coordinate on climate action. By embedding talent in high-leverage roles and connecting those roles through a responsive learning and coordination network, CR is helping rebuild a climate ecosystem that is more resilient, distributed, and built to last.

item.content:encoded:
The IDB Group is a community of diverse, versatile, and passionate people who come together on a journey to improve lives in Latin America and the Caribbean. Our people find purpose and do what they love in an inclusive, collaborative, agile, and rewarding environment.

About this position

​​We are looking for a motivated, technically rigorous, and collaborative Data Scientist. As Data Scientist, you will contribute to build a modern, AI-enabled data infrastructure that allows the Bank to harmonize, process, and analyze large-scale household survey data from across Latin America and the Caribbean efficiently and transparently. You will also help develop state-of-the-art tools and methods to improve how the IDB measures poverty and income distribution in the region, and to strengthen how it measures the poverty focus of its projects.

You will work in the Poverty Group, part of the Social Sector. This team is responsible for expanding knowledge on poverty and inequality in the region and on the policies that can speed up their reduction, in support of the IDB Group’s Institutional Strategy, IDBImpact+, and its goal of ensuring that a significant share of IDB projects directly benefit people living in poverty.

What you’ll do

-​Contribute to the harmonization of household surveys and other microdata across Latin America and the Caribbean, designing and implementing AI-assisted workflows, for example using large language models to map questionnaires and variables across countries and years, classify occupations and industries, and generate and document harmonization code, with systematic human validation and a transparent, documented, and traceable methodology.

-Provide technical and operational support in the design, development, and maintenance of scalable cloud-based data infrastructure (e.g., AWS S3 and Databricks) for storing, processing, and managing large-scale survey, census, administrative, and geospatial data. Additionally, support the implementation of automated pipelines to update harmonized databases as new data becomes available.

-Support the implementation and coordination of automated quality-control and validation procedures for harmonized data and indicators, including consistency checks across countries and over time, AI-assisted anomaly detection, and benchmarking against official statistics.

-Contribute to the computation, updating, and monitoring of poverty, inequality, and other social indicators using tools such as Python, R, and Stata, helping ensure the reproducibility and comparability of results across countries.

-Support the development of poverty-targeting tools for IDB projects, such as poverty maps that combine survey, census, geospatial, and other non-traditional data using small area estimation and machine learning methods.

-Conduct statistical and econometric analyses to derive policy-relevant insights and support decision-making in project design.

-Make data and tools accessible to teams across the Bank through documentation, metadata catalogs, and user-facing tools (e.g., APIs or dashboards), and support training of colleagues in AI-assisted data workflows.

-Support other activities of the data and digital social cluster as agreed with the SCL supervisor.

What you’ll need

• Education: Bachelor’s degree in economics, statistics, data science, computer science, or a related quantitative field.
